novel_mechanics_found: Level 4 introduces two simultaneously checked perpendicular chain/guide pairs. The color-10 vertical chain at x=23 must see 9 -> 14, while the color-11 vertical chain at x=35 must see 8 -> 12. The horizontal carrier initially contains segments beneath all four rack blocks, so retraction is not merely undo: shortening its reach selectively decouples already-correct blocks. A block pinned on a vertical segment can remain in place while a horizontal segment retracts through it, allowing the x=35 pair to stay complete while the x=23 pair is lifted and restaged.

A source-grounded ACTION1-4 transition model then searched only legal settled states without consuming env.step calls; its 25-action tail reached the exact simultaneous predicate {10:[9,14], 11:[8,12]}. Direct game-logic execution independently confirmed the predicate and armed the success animation. gotchas: L4 has two independent ordering strips, not one combined four-color strip: color-10 requires 9 then 14, and color-11 requires 8 then 12.
Both vertical predicates must hold simultaneously; completing one pair and then dragging it away loses progress.
The active horizontal chain starts with segments hidden beneath every rack block, so early vertical movement can carry the whole row even when only one segment is visually obvious.
Horizontal retraction can pass through a block pinned by a perpendicular vertical segment; this selective decoupling is essential for preserving the completed x=35 pair.
The winning action resolves the success animation and returns the next level in the same env.step call, so the decisive evidence is frame_level changing 3 -> 4.
The reported 273 env.step calls include the mandatory prefix gate, five live mapping actions, one additional 81-label planner-state replay, and the final 106-label fresh reproduction gate.
